metadata.description: Comprehensive test questions for RAG evaluation covering answer quality, retrieval accuracy, and edge cases
metadata.notes: Designed to evaluate RAG systems across multiple dimensions including retrieval, answer quality, and groundedness

questions.question: What is the recommended daily protein intake for sedentary adults?
questions.expected_answer: 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight

questions.question: How much fiber should women consume daily?
questions.expected_answer: 25 grams

questions.question: What percentage of daily calories should come from fats?
questions.expected_answer: 20-35% of daily calories

questions.question: Which vitamin is produced by the skin when exposed to sunlight?
questions.expected_answer: Vitamin D

questions.question: What nutrient must vegans supplement?
questions.expected_answer: Vitamin B12

questions.question: How much iron do women of reproductive age need daily?
questions.expected_answer: 18 mg

questions.question: What is the primary fat source in the Mediterranean diet?
questions.expected_answer: Olive oil

questions.question: How many grams of carbs are allowed daily on the keto diet?
questions.expected_answer: 20-50 grams

questions.question: What does the plate method suggest for vegetables?
questions.expected_answer: Fill half your plate with vegetables

questions.question: What is the 16:8 intermittent fasting approach?
questions.expected_answer: 16 hours fasting, 8 hours eating

questions.question: I'm feeling tired all the time as a vegetarian woman. What nutrients might I be missing?
questions.expected_answer: Iron and vitamin B12 are common deficiencies that cause fatigue in vegetarian women

questions.question: What helps my body absorb calcium better?
questions.expected_answer: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption

questions.question: I want to improve my brain health. What foods should I eat?
questions.expected_answer: Fatty fish like salmon rich in omega-3s (EPA and DHA) support brain health

questions.question: What should I eat after working out for muscle recovery?
questions.expected_answer: Carbs to replenish glycogen and protein for muscle recovery within 30-60 minutes

questions.question: How can I lower my blood pressure through diet?
questions.expected_answer: Follow DASH diet, reduce sodium to less than 2300mg, increase potassium, eat fruits and vegetables

questions.question: What's the best protein source for someone who can't eat meat?
questions.expected_answer: Legumes, tofu, tempeh, quinoa, and other plant proteins

questions.question: How do omega-3s and omega-6s affect inflammation, and what's the ideal ratio?
questions.expected_answer: Omega-3s reduce inflammation while excessive omega-6s promote it. Optimal ratio is 4:1 or lower.

questions.question: What are all the nutrients I need to monitor on a vegan diet and their sources?
questions.expected_answer: B12 (supplements), D (fortified/sun), omega-3 (algae/seeds), iron (legumes), zinc (nuts/seeds), calcium (fortified milk/tofu)

questions.question: Compare the Mediterranean, DASH, and heart-healthy diets for cardiovascular health.
questions.expected_answer: All three emphasize fruits, vegetables, whole grains. Mediterranean focuses on olive oil and fish, DASH on sodium restriction, heart-healthy on limiting saturated/trans fats.

questions.question: How do different B vitamins work together and what are their sources?
questions.expected_answer: B vitamins work together in metabolic pathways. Found in whole grains, meat, eggs, legumes, leafy greens. B12 only in animal products.

questions.question: What's the relationship between gut health and mental health?
questions.expected_answer: Gut-brain axis connects digestive tract and brain. 95% of serotonin made in gut. Microbiome affects mood through neural, hormonal, immune pathways.

questions.question: EPA DHA brain inflammation
questions.expected_answer: EPA and DHA omega-3 fatty acids reduce inflammation and support brain health

questions.question: sunshine vitamin bones calcium
questions.expected_answer: Vitamin D is produced by sunlight exposure and is crucial for calcium absorption and bone health

questions.question: keto flu constipation side effects
questions.expected_answer: Potential side effects of ketogenic diet include keto flu, constipation, and nutrient deficiencies

questions.question: oxalates leafy green cooking reduces
questions.expected_answer: Spinach is high in oxalates which inhibit mineral absorption; cooking reduces oxalate content

questions.question: methylcobalamin cyanocobalamin absorption age
questions.expected_answer: Methylcobalamin and cyanocobalamin are B12 supplement forms. Absorption decreases with age.

questions.expected_answer: NOT_IN_CONTEXT

questions.question: What's the best programming language?
questions.expected_answer: NOT_IN_CONTEXT

questions.question: Tell me about the history of ancient Rome
questions.expected_answer: NOT_IN_CONTEXT

questions.question: Is eating 10 eggs per day safe?
questions.expected_answer: Most guidelines allow up to 3 eggs daily; 10 eggs exceeds recommendations

questions.question: Can I survive on a diet of only potatoes?
questions.expected_answer: No, a potato-only diet would lack complete protein, B12, and other essential nutrients

questions.question: What if I'm both diabetic and trying to do keto?
questions.expected_answer: Keto may help blood sugar control but requires medical supervision for diabetics

questions.question: Is it safe to take 10,000 IU of vitamin D daily?
questions.expected_answer: High doses require medical supervision; recommended is 600-800 IU, though some suggest higher doses

questions.question: Can children follow a ketogenic diet?
questions.expected_answer: Keto requires medical supervision and may not be appropriate for growing children

questions.question: Hey, what should I eat?
questions.expected_answer: For a balanced meal: half vegetables, quarter protein, quarter whole grains, plus healthy fats

questions.question: Is it good or bad?
questions.expected_answer: UNCLEAR_QUERY

questions.question: What about vitamins?
questions.expected_answer: Various vitamins serve different purposes. More context needed for specific advice.

questions.question: What do you think about the diet?
questions.expected_answer: UNCLEAR_QUERY

questions.question: I heard eggs are dangerous. Should I never eat them?
questions.expected_answer: Recent research shows dietary cholesterol in eggs has minimal impact on blood cholesterol for most people. Up to 3 eggs daily is generally fine.

questions.question: Carbs are bad and should be eliminated completely, right?
questions.expected_answer: No, carbs are the body's primary energy source. Complex carbs provide essential nutrients. Adults should get 45-65% of calories from carbs.

questions.question: All fats make you fat, don't they?
questions.expected_answer: No, dietary fats are essential for hormone production, nutrient absorption, and cell membranes. Unsaturated fats are heart-healthy.

questions.question: How much water should I drink daily?
questions.expected_answer: General recommendation is 8 cups (64 ounces) daily, though needs vary by activity, climate, and body size.

questions.question: What is the glycemic index and why does it matter?
questions.expected_answer: GI ranks carbs by how quickly they raise blood sugar (0-100 scale). Low GI foods provide stable energy and help manage diabetes.

questions.question: Explain the difference between soluble and insoluble fiber
questions.expected_answer: Soluble fiber dissolves in water, forms gel, slows digestion, lowers cholesterol. Insoluble adds bulk, promotes regular bowel movements.

questions.question: What are probiotics and prebiotics?
questions.expected_answer: Probiotics are live beneficial bacteria (yogurt, kefir). Prebiotics are fibers that feed beneficial bacteria (garlic, onions, oats).

questions.question: What nutrients do pregnant women need more of?
questions.expected_answer: Folic acid (400-800mcg), iron (27mg), calcium (1000mg), vitamin D (600 IU), DHA omega-3 (200-300mg)

questions.question: How do nutritional needs change for older adults?
questions.expected_answer: Caloric needs decrease but nutrient needs stay high. Increase protein (1.0-1.2g/kg), vitamin D (800-1000 IU), B12 via supplements.

questions.question: What are the eight major food allergens?
questions.expected_answer: Milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, wheat, soy, fish, and shellfish

questions.question: How much vitamin C do I need and what are good sources?
questions.expected_answer: 75-90mg daily for adults. Sources: citrus fruits, bell peppers, strawberries, broccoli, kiwi.
